prompt: An accessibility ramp rises $2$ ft over a horizontal run of $24$ ft. Building codes cap the ramp angle at $4.8^\circ$. What angle does this ramp make with the ground, rounded to the nearest tenth of a degree?
hint: Rise is opposite the ramp angle and run is adjacent — that is tangent.

hints.text: Rise is opposite the ramp angle and run is adjacent — that is tangent.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try a friendly ratio: a rise of $1$ over a run of $1$ gives $\tan \theta = 1$, so $\theta = \tan^{-1}(1) = 45^\circ$. Notice the final move is the inverse tangent, not the ratio itself.
$\tan \theta = \frac{2}{24} \approx 0.0833$. That decimal is the ratio, not the angle.

explanation: Set up the ratio with the angle at the bottom of the ramp: opposite $= 2$ (rise), adjacent $= 24$ (run).
Undo the tangent: $\theta = \tan^{-1}(0.0833) \approx 4.8^\circ$ — the ramp just barely passes code. Choice B.

alternativeExplanations.title: Sanity check with a picture
steps: A ramp that creeps up $2$ ft while stretching $24$ ft forward is nearly flat.
Nearly flat means a tiny angle — a handful of degrees, which points straight at $4.8^\circ$.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: Choice A, $0.1^\circ$, is what you get by reporting $\tan \theta \approx 0.083$ as if it were the angle and rounding — the calculator gave you the RATIO, and you still owe it a $\tan^{-1}$. Choice C, $85.2^\circ$, comes from flipping the fraction to $\frac{24}{2}$, which finds the angle at the TOP of the ramp instead.
Fix both by naming the angle before you compute: stand at the bottom corner, check that the rise is across from you and the run runs away from you, then finish with $\tan^{-1}$.
